D.t: Mark Warner leads by 20.9 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 773,428 votes; a one point swing is about 18,547 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +13.8 and D +28.1. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Fairfax County, a projected net 260,439 votes; Arlington County, a projected net 79,429 votes; Richmond city, a projected net 74,341 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.

The large counties within 12 points: Spotsylvania County, D +3.4, 1.7% of the vote; Roanoke County, R +8.0, 1.2% of the vote; Fauquier County, R +7.6, 0.9% of the vote; York County, D +4.0, 0.9% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Mark Warner runs furthest behind in Bedford County, Hanover County, Suffolk city. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 71% of voters, 52 to 44, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.56 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 66% of voters, 59 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.29 points; Voters without a degree, 52% of voters, 55 to 41, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.60 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Mark Warner: Immigration voters 24 to 73, Small counties 43 to 54, White voters 52 to 44. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$7.5M cash against $230K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.4 points away from Mark Warner. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.

National tide: Gallup party identification moved from Republicans 48 Democrats 45 in the third quarter of 2024 to Democrats 50 Republicans 39 in the third quarter of 2026, 14 points toward the Democrats.
